response.sql: WITH ch AS (SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.orderbase HAVING AVG(f.feerate) IS NOT NULL), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS bench FROM ch) SELECT AVG(ch.avg_rate) AS mean_avg_fee_rate_above_benchmark, AVG(ch.avg_rate - b.bench) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark FROM ch CROSS JOIN b WHERE ch.avg_rate > b.bench

assumptions.assumption: Channels are distinct orders.orderbase values; orders with NULL orderbase form no channel but are grouped as one NULL group unless excluded. Here NULL-channel group is treated as a channel only if it has non-null rates (it is not filtered out).
Channel average is computed over all fee rows (fee-level mean, not per-order mean); channels with no non-null feerate are excluded from the benchmark.
If no channel exceeds the benchmark (e.g., all equal), the query returns a single row with NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude orders with a NULL orderbase from being treated as a channel.
alternatives.sql: WITH ch AS (SELECT o.orderbase, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE o.orderbase IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.orderbase HAVING AVG(f.feerate) IS NOT NULL), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS bench FROM ch) SELECT AVG(ch.avg_rate) AS mean_avg_fee_rate_above_benchmark, AVG(ch.avg_rate - b.bench) AS mean_excess_over_benchmark FROM ch CROSS JOIN b WHERE ch.avg_rate > b.bench
